title: Versal formal objects detect unobstructedness by adic formal smoothness
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where local means having a unique maximal ideal. Let $k$ be a finite extension of $R/\mathfrak m_R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ be the category of Artinian local $R$-algebras with specified residue field $k$, with local maps inducing the identity on $k$; Artinian means descending chains of ideals stabilize. Let $\mathcal F$ be a pseudofunctor from $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ to groupoids, so it assigns groupoids and extension-of-base functors with coherent composition isomorphisms, and suppose $\mathcal F(k)$ has exactly one arrow between any two objects and is nonempty. Let $C$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field $k$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\xi_n\in\mathcal F(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$, $n\geq1$, be objects with coherent transition isomorphisms. For a local residue-preserving map $u:C\to A$, write $\xi_u$ for its pullback from a sufficiently large truncation, and put $h_C(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_{R,\mathrm{loc},\mathrm{cont}}(C,A)$, where continuity means killing some power of $\mathfrak m_C$. Assume versality: for every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$, $u\in h_C(A)$, $\eta'\in\mathcal F(A')$, and isomorphism $\eta'|_A\cong\xi_u$, there exist $u'\in h_C(A')$ lifting $u$ and an isomorphism $\eta'\cong\xi_{u'}$ inducing the prescribed one. Then every object of $\mathcal F(A)$ lifts up to isomorphism along every surjection $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ if and only if $R\to C$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic].

source.place: Tag 0DZK, lemma-smooth-power-series-classical, (1) iff (2); definitions definition-CLambda, definition-predeformation-category and definition-versal (Tag 06HR).

proof.text: Every $\eta\in\mathcal F(A)$ is induced by a map from $C$. Indeed let $u_0:C\to k$ be the specified residue map, which kills $\mathfrak m_C$ and belongs to $h_C(k)$. The hypothesis on $\mathcal F(k)$ gives an isomorphism $\eta|_k\cong\xi_{u_0}$. Apply the assumed versality to the surjection $A\twoheadrightarrow k$, this map $u_0$, the object $\eta$, and that isomorphism. It supplies $u:C\to A$ in $h_C(A)$ and an isomorphism $\eta\cong\xi_u$. This proves the Artinian essential-surjectivity assertion directly from the hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0DZK, lemma-smooth-power-series-classical, proof of (1) iff (2); Tag 06HT, lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial, restricted to Artinian objects.

proof.text: Assume $\mathcal F$ is unobstructed. For any surjection $p:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ in $\mathcal C_{R,k}$ and $u\in h_C(A)$, unobstructedness applied to $\xi_u$ gives $\eta'\in\mathcal F(A')$ and an isomorphism $\eta'|_A\cong\xi_u$. Versality applied to precisely these data supplies $u'\in h_C(A')$ with $p\circ u'=u$. Thus $h_C(A')\to h_C(A)$ is surjective for every such $p$. The implication from this lifting property to adic formal smoothness in [lem-sfb-adic-smooth-fixed-residue-lifting] now applies to the given complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $C$ with the specified residue field $k$.

source.place: Tag 0DZK, lemma-smooth-power-series-classical, forward implication, with Tag 0DYL, lemma-smooth, (1) implies (2).

proof.text: Conversely suppose $R\to C$ is adically formally smooth. Fix a surjection $p:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ and $\eta\in\mathcal F(A)$. Step 1 gives $u\in h_C(A)$ and $\eta\cong\xi_u$. The opposite implication of [lem-sfb-adic-smooth-fixed-residue-lifting] supplies $u'\in h_C(A')$ with $p\circ u'=u$. Take $\eta'=\xi_{u'}$. Coherence of the formal object and its base-change functors gives $\eta'|_A\cong\xi_{p\circ u'}=\xi_u\cong\eta$. Thus every object lifts along every surjection, as required. Only existence up to isomorphism is needed here; no uniqueness or algebraization of the formal object is used.

source.place: Tag 0DZK, lemma-smooth-power-series-classical, reverse implication; Tag 06HT, lemma-versal-object-quasi-initial, in the Artinian case.
